title: Terraform-driven lifecycle scripts and alert playbook for VPC node degradation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a robust, Terraform-driven runbook and automation layer to detect and remediate common Private (VPC) deployment health degradations. Goals: codify checks for node/network/service-level drift, provide safe automated remediation paths (instance replacement, route/security reconciliation, cert refresh), and integrate with alerts/incident flow so platform teams can opt into automated fixes while preserving auditability.
background: Incidents over the last two quarters show repeated VPC node degradation patterns: kernel conntrack exhaustion after large rollout, stale route table entries after maintenance, and intermittent node-cert expiry causing gRPC failures. Current runbooks are ad-hoc; we need deterministic Terraform/IaC-driven steps plus non-destructive prechecks and post-smoke validations.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A Terraform module (tf-mod-vpc-selfheal) exposes lifecycle scripts and a 'plan-and-safety-check' workflow for node replacement
2) Automated remediation playbook can be invoked from PagerDuty/Slack with RBAC gating and a change PR created when destructive changes are needed
3) Post-remediation smoke tests (health checks, latency SLO validation, KV cache warmup) run automatically and report to Console
4) All automated actions produce audit entries (GitHub PR + Terraform run logs + Console events) for compliance
5) New alert rules detect the three common failure classes and map to specific runbook play actions
monitoring_alerts: vpc.route_table_inconsistency detected after apply -> severity P2
remediation_steps: A. Automated non-destructive prechecks: check Terraform plan drift, verify node kubelet/gRPC health, confirm route table & SG consistency, snapshot current state (tfstate + monitoring snapshot)
B. If conntrack saturation: run conntrack flush helper on targeted nodes; if saturation persists, trigger node cordon -> drain -> replace (Terraform taint + apply) with concurrency limit=1
C. If gRPC cert expiry: attempt on-node cert rotate script (non-destructive), otherwise create a Terraform change to roll certs across nodes in canary batches
D. If route table inconsistency: run reconciliation module to reattach correct routes, then verify connectivity matrix with synthetic probes
E. If Terraform state lock or corruption: follow tfstate recovery play: promote backup state, unlock with sentinel checks, notify infra-owners, and run plan in dry-run mode before apply
F. Post-remediation: run smoke tests (tokenized generation across 3 models, KV cache warmup, 99th-p latency check), publish results to Console and close alert only if smoke passes
automation_playbook: tf-mod-vpc-selfheal: Terraform module that encapsulates lifecycle hooks (precheck, remediation_apply, postvalidate) and exposes a 'dry_run=true' safe flag
lifecycle-scripts: small Go binaries installed on private agents to run infra-safe commands (conntrack-flush, cert-rotate, health-probe) invoked via SSM or kube exec

orchestrator: a Lambda (or k8s job) that accepts an alert webhook, runs prechecks, evaluates automated remediation policy, and either executes remediation or opens a draft GitHub PR with proposed Terraform changes
policy engine: selector rules to decide automated vs manual (based on customer tier, change window, incident frequency); decisions are logged and reversible
audit: every remediation produces a GitHub PR (if changes to IaC are required) and a terraform run link; ephemeral logs forwarded to Console's private deployment events stream
rollback_procedures: If remediation increases error rate or fails smoke tests within 10 minutes -> automatically revert Terraform apply using stored plan or use backup tfstate snapshot
If node replacement causes >5% capacity loss for a region -> pause remediation, scale up temporary capacity pool (if available) and re-run replacement with smaller concurrency
Manual escalation path: page platform on-call, include runbook link, relevant PR link, and collected prechecks
roles_and_routing: PagerDuty mapping: P1 alerts -> infra-platform on-call; automated remediation is gated by 'auto-remediate' flag per-service
Slack flows: #infra-alerts posts a runbook card with 'Run automated remediation' and 'Open manual playbook' buttons; actions create a GitHub PR when applicable
RBAC: only ops-admins and the remediation-bot identity can apply Terraform changes to production state; all actions require MFA & SSO audit entry
notes_and_decisions: Decision 2026-03-05: use GitHub PRs as the single source of truth for any IaC mutation triggered by automation
Decision 2026-03-02: implement non-destructive 'dry_run' flow as default; auto-remediate only for conntrack and cert refresh scenarios initially
Trade-off: full automated node replacement reduces time-to-fix but increases blast radius; mitigate via strict concurrency and post-smoke gating
